toxicities: High doses may cause nausea, vomiting, rash, and fever. IV administration may cause anaphylactoid reactions. Potentially hepatotoxic when taken 4 hours after alcohol consumption.
summary: N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) is a precursor to the antioxidant glutathione, used medically for acetaminophen overdose and as a mucolytic. It is being researched for psychiatric conditions including addiction, OCD, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder.
effectsSummary: Appetite suppression, cough suppression, bronchodilation, increased motivation, anxiety suppression, focus enhancement, addiction suppression, anti-inflammatory effects.
dosageRemark: Safe oral dosage ranges from 300mg to 3000mg daily depending on individual factors and health conditions. Oral bioavailability is approximately 4%.
generalRisks: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, rash, and fever. IV administration may cause allergic reactions. High-dose animal studies suggest potential cardiac and pulmonary damage, though at doses far exceeding human use.
longtermRisks: Long-term effects are not well studied. May cause gastrointestinal issues at high doses. Can worsen liver damage if taken 4 hours after alcohol consumption.
saferUse: Do not take after consuming alcohol
Consult a doctor if on other medications
